// Parsed by TestVerdictGuardCatches, never compiled. Lines marked "// want" must be reported;
// every other use of the verdict here is a comparison, a case or a map key, and is allowed.
package bad

import (
	"fmt"

	w "github.com/deedglass/deedglass/internal/witness"
)

func decide() w.Verdict {
	return w.Verified // want
}

func assign() string {
	v := w.Verdict("")
	v = w.Verified // want
	s := "VERIFIED" // want
	_ = v
	return s
}

var pinned = w.Verified // want

type claim struct{ Verdict w.Verdict }

func literal() []claim {
	return []claim{{Verdict: w.Verified}} // want
}

func element() []string {
	return []string{"MISMATCH", `VERIFIED`} // want
}

func argument() {
	fmt.Println((w.Verified)) // want
}

func send(c chan string) {
	c <- "VERIFIED" // want
}

// Allowed: comparisons, cases and lookup keys.
func allowed(v w.Verdict, s string) int {
	if v == w.Verified || s != "VERIFIED" {
		return 1
	}
	switch s {
	case "VERIFIED":
		return 2
	}
	switch v {
	case w.Verified:
		return 3
	}
	glyph := map[string]string{"VERIFIED": "ok"}
	return len(glyph[s])
}

// Allowed: conversions inside comparisons and cases (cmd/deedglass/witness.go does this).
func converted(v string) bool {
	switch v {
	case string(w.Verified):
		return true
	}
	return v == string((w.Verified)) || w.Verdict(v) != w.Verified
}

// Reported: a conversion that produces the value.
func produced() string {
	return string(w.Verified) // want
}

func passed(f func(w.Verdict)) {
	f(w.Verdict("VERIFIED")) // want
}
